title: Gap Support
teaches: Gap Support as we trade it: a leader gaps up, price drifts back days or weeks later to the gap-up day's low (not the prior day's high) while the gap is still open, holds it or breaches it slightly, and closes back over it in the upper half of the test day; above a flat or rising 50-day and the 200-day; the stop sits a few cents under the test day's low; a third comes off at 3R, another at 5R, the rest on the 10-day or 21-day trail, and a loss taken at the stop is the system working.

questions.q: Which line does Gap Support defend?
choices: The gap-up day's low
The prior day's high
The record-volume day's close
The 200-day line
questions.answer: The gap-up day's low
questions.why: The gap-up day's low. The line is the low of the gap-up day, not the gap-fill spot, which is the prior day's high.
questions.lesson_line: The line is the gap-up day's low.

wrong.The prior day's high: That is the gap-fill spot. It sits below the line, and it is not what we defend.
wrong.The record-volume day's close: That is the High Volume Edge's line, a different setup.
wrong.The 200-day line: The 200-day is a filter for the test day, not the line.

questions.q: The gap day itself is Gap Support.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The gap day itself is a PEG. A gap that is never revisited is nothing. The setup is the later test of the gap-up low.
questions.lesson_line: The gap day is a PEG. The later test is Gap Support.

questions.q: A Gap Support test day may close under the 200-day if the 50-day is rising.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The test day closes above the 200-day SMA. No longs below the 200-day simple moving average, unless it is a parabolic long.
questions.lesson_line: Under the 200-day, there is no Gap Support to buy.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The stop goes a few cents under the test day's ___.
questions.answer: low
questions.why: Low. The stop sits a few cents under the test day's low.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first: a few cents under the test day's low.

questions.q: In which market reading do we take only A+ gap tests?
choices: Orange
Green
Yellow
Red
questions.answer: Orange
questions.why: Orange. Green is full risk, Yellow is smaller and fewer, Orange is A+ only, and Red is mostly cash and shorts.
questions.lesson_line: Orange means A+ only.

wrong.Green: Green is full risk for every grade.
wrong.Yellow: Yellow is smaller and fewer, not A+ only.
wrong.Red: Red is mostly cash and shorts, with no new longs.

questions.q: Gap Support buys are limit orders set just under the line.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Entries are market orders, as on every setup.
questions.lesson_line: Market orders, regular hours.

questions.q: What makes an up gap a true gap?
choices: Its low is above the prior high
The open is above the prior close
Volume doubles the average
The close is above the day's open
questions.answer: Its low is above the prior high
questions.why: The whole day trades above the prior high. A true gap has the gap day's low above the prior day's high.
questions.lesson_line: A true gap leaves a hole above yesterday's high.

wrong.The open is above the prior close: That can happen with the low back inside the prior day's range; a true gap needs more.
wrong.The close is above the day's open: A close above the open says nothing about a hole.

questions.q: When is the gap still open?
choices: No close at or under prior high
No trade under the gap-up low
Green closes every day since
Volume stays above average since
questions.answer: No close at or under prior high
questions.why: No close at or under the prior day's high since the gap day. That prior high is the gap-fill spot.
questions.lesson_line: Open means no close back at the gap-fill spot.

wrong.No trade under the gap-up low: A slight trade under the gap-up low is allowed; the gap-fill spot is the test.
wrong.Green closes every day since: Red days are fine while the gap stays open.
wrong.Volume stays above average since: Volume does not decide whether a gap is open.

questions.q: A close at or under the prior day's high means the gap filled and the setup is dead.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A close at or under the gap-fill spot means the gap filled and the setup is dead. Buyable gap-ups do not close their gaps.
questions.lesson_line: A close at the gap-fill spot kills it.

questions.q: A gap out of a downtrend, under a falling 50-day, is not Gap Support.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. No downtrend gaps: the gap day closes above a flat or rising 50-day. Morales: not while the stock is in a downtrend.
questions.lesson_line: No downtrend gaps.

questions.q: Why not put the stop under the gap-fill spot?
choices: It is about 6% away at the median
It is too close to the entry price
It sits above the gap-up day's low
It moves with the day's volume
questions.answer: It is about 6% away at the median
questions.why: It is far away. A stop under the gap-fill spot is a median 6% away, only 12% within 3%, and it wins less often per R.
questions.lesson_line: Stop under the test day's low, not the fill spot.

wrong.It is too close to the entry price: It is the opposite: the fill spot is usually far from the entry.
wrong.It sits above the gap-up day's low: The fill spot is below the gap-up low on a true gap, not above it.
wrong.It moves with the day's volume: A level does not move with volume.

questions.q: Heavy-volume selling into the line is a warning, and a quiet pullback is the version traders like best.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Heavy-volume selling into the line is a warning. A quiet pullback on lighter volume is the version traders like best.
questions.lesson_line: Quiet pullbacks to the line are the best ones.

questions.q: Where should the test day close?
choices: Back over the line, in the upper half
Right at the day's low
Under the line, in the lower half
At the prior day's high
questions.answer: Back over the line, in the upper half
questions.why: Back over the line, in the upper half of its range. A lower wick or a hammer is the look.
questions.lesson_line: A lower wick and a strong close at the line.

wrong.Right at the day's low: A close at the low is a day still falling.
wrong.Under the line, in the lower half: A close under the line is not a hold.
wrong.At the prior day's high: The prior day's high is the gap-fill spot, far below the line.

questions.q: Gap Support is bought at full size at one price with one stop, and we never add.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Full size at one price with one stop. A gap test is a new trade, not an add.
questions.lesson_line: One buy, one price, one stop.

questions.q: The stop sits in a real stop order with the broker, and it only moves up.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A real stop order with the broker, not a stop kept in your head. It only moves up.
questions.lesson_line: A real stop order, and it only moves up.

questions.q: Gap-up low 53.03, test-day low 52.45. How deep is the breach, in percent?
questions.why: 1.1. The gap-up low minus the test-day low, divided by the gap-up low. ILMN's slight undercut was this deep and still closed back near its high.
questions.lesson_line: Breach depth is the dip under the line, over the line.

questions.q: Bought at 25.10 with the stop at 24.71. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 26.27. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add three of those to the fill. AKAM ran to 30.4R from these levels.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the close. The first third comes off there.

questions.q: What does the post-gap high do to the first third?
choices: A cue to sell it early; 3R is the rule
It replaces 3R as the first-third spot
It moves the first third out to 5R
Nothing; it is not part of the plan
questions.answer: A cue to sell it early; 3R is the rule
questions.why: A cue to sell early. By our current default, the first third is a third at 3R. The post-gap high can tell you to take that third early.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R is the rule. The post-gap high is a cue to take it early.

wrong.It replaces 3R as the first-third spot: By our current default the plan stays a third at 3R. The post-gap high does not replace it.
wrong.It moves the first third out to 5R: The second third is at 5R. The post-gap high does not push the first one out.
wrong.Nothing; it is not part of the plan: It is a cue. When it comes before 3R, you may take the first third early.

questions.q: Where does the stop go on a Gap Support buy?
choices: Just under the test day's low
Under the gap-fill spot for room
Exactly on the gap-up day's low
A fixed 2% under the gap-up low
questions.answer: Just under the test day's low
questions.why: A few cents under the test day's low. Not under the gap-fill spot, and not a fixed cushion under the gap-up low.
questions.lesson_line: Stop a few cents under the test day's low.

wrong.Under the gap-fill spot for room: That stop is a median 6% away.
wrong.Exactly on the gap-up day's low: The stop sits a few cents under a real low, not on a line.
wrong.A fixed 2% under the gap-up low: A fixed 1% to 3% cushion is not our stop.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The stop moves to breakeven at the first ___ by default.
questions.answer: trim
questions.why: Trim. The stop moves to breakeven between 2R and 5R, and by default at the first trim.
questions.lesson_line: First trim, then the stop to breakeven.

questions.q: The last third trails a close under the 21-day for a fast mover or the 10-day for a steadier one.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. It is the other way round. Sell the last third on a close under the 10-day for a fast mover or the 21-day for a steadier one.
questions.lesson_line: Trail the last third under the 10- or 21-day.

questions.q: How far must price pull back before the test?
choices: At least 1 ATR under the post-gap high
At least 10% under the post-gap high
Any dip at all
Back to the prior close
questions.answer: At least 1 ATR under the post-gap high
questions.why: At least 1 ATR under the post-gap high. The close before the test sits at least 1 ATR under the post-gap high.
questions.lesson_line: A real pullback is at least one ATR deep.

wrong.At least 10% under the post-gap high: The measure is in ATRs, not a fixed percent.
wrong.Any dip at all: A shallow dip is not a pullback to the line.
wrong.Back to the prior close: Back to the prior close is the gap-fill spot; that kills the setup.

questions.q: Fill 15.96, stop 15.48. How far is the stop from the fill, in percent?
questions.why: 3.0. The fill minus the stop, divided by the fill. That sits right at the usual 3% limit. VIAV had these levels.
questions.lesson_line: Stop distance is the fill minus the stop, over the fill.

questions.q: Buy the close?
questions.story: The test day undercut the gap-up low by 4% and closed 3% under it.
choices: No buy; the close is under the line
Buy; the undercut reclaims later
Buy half size at the close
Buy the close, stop at the gap fill
questions.answer: No buy; the close is under the line
questions.why: No buy. The test day undercut the line and closed under it. A later close under the gap-up low with no reclaim is a failed gap.
questions.lesson_line: A close under the line is not a hold.

wrong.Buy; the undercut reclaims later: Hoping for a reclaim later is how a failed gap becomes a loss.
wrong.Buy half size at the close: Half size on a failed test is still a failed test.
wrong.Buy the close, stop at the gap fill: A stop at the gap-fill spot is far wider than the rules allow.

questions.q: Buy the close?
questions.story: At 3:55 the stock sits on the gap-up low but is still making new lows for the day.
choices: No; it is still falling into the close
Yes; it is right on the line
Yes, with a tight stop
Yes; the gap is still open
questions.answer: No; it is still falling into the close
questions.why: No. A test day still falling into the close, with no hold and no reclaim, is not the setup.
questions.lesson_line: No hold and no reclaim means no buy.

wrong.Yes; it is right on the line: Sitting on the line is not enough; the day must hold and close back strong.
wrong.Yes, with a tight stop: A tight stop does not fix a day still falling.
wrong.Yes; the gap is still open: The gap being open is one test; the hold is another.

questions.q: What is the plan for the first third?
questions.story: You bought a test at 53.27 with the stop at 52.40. The post-gap high is 55.63, just under 3R.
choices: A third at 3R, 55.88; 55.63 is a cue
A third at the post-gap high, always
At 5R; skip the first third
Hold everything for the trail
questions.answer: A third at 3R, 55.88; 55.63 is a cue
questions.why: A third at 3R, 55.88. By our current default, 3R is the rule and the post-gap high at 55.63 is a cue to take that third early.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R. The post-gap high is a cue to take it early.

wrong.A third at the post-gap high, always: By our current default the rule stays a third at 3R. The post-gap high is a cue, not a new rule.
wrong.At 5R; skip the first third: The first third comes off at 3R. The 5R third is the second one.
wrong.Hold everything for the trail: The first third is sold at 3R. Only the last third rides the trail.

questions.q: Buy or pass?
questions.story: You planned to buy the test day's close at 50.00 but were away from your desk. The next morning the stock opens at 52.30.
choices: Pass; over 4% past the buy point
Buy, the hold is confirmed
Buy half size to limit the risk
Buy with a wider stop to fit it
questions.answer: Pass; over 4% past the buy point
questions.why: Pass. 52.30 is more than 4% over the 50.00 buy point. Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays put and the shares shrink.
questions.lesson_line: Miss it rather than chase it. Four percent and done.

wrong.Buy, the hold is confirmed: Confirmed and too far away are both true. The chase line is 4%.
wrong.Buy half size to limit the risk: Half of a bad entry is still a bad entry.
wrong.Buy with a wider stop to fit it: A wider stop to fit a late entry is the mistake, not the fix.

questions.q: Buy the test?
questions.story: A clean test day closes back over the line on Wednesday. The company reports Thursday after the close.
choices: No; a report is within 3 sessions
Yes; the test day is clean
Yes, but at half size only
Yes, and hold through the report
questions.answer: No; a report is within 3 sessions
questions.why: No. We take no new buy in the 3 sessions before an earnings report. A test long after the gap can land near the next report.
questions.lesson_line: A report in 3 sessions or less means no new buy.

wrong.Yes; the test day is clean: A clean chart does not remove the report risk.
wrong.Yes, but at half size only: Half size is still a new buy in the report window.
wrong.Yes, and hold through the report: Holding through a report needs 5R, not a new position.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: The test day's low puts the honest stop 5% from the fill. A friend says to put it 1.5% under the fill so the size looks normal.
choices: Size down by the formula, or skip
Put the stop 1.5% under the fill
Buy full size anyway
Put the stop at the gap-fill spot
questions.answer: Size down by the formula, or skip
questions.why: Size down by the formula, or skip. The honest stop stays under the test day's low. Pulling it in is never the fix.
questions.lesson_line: If the honest stop does not fit, size down or skip.

wrong.Put the stop 1.5% under the fill: Pulling the stop in to fit the size is the mistake, not the plan.
wrong.Buy full size anyway: Full size on a stop that wide breaks the risk rule.
wrong.Put the stop at the gap-fill spot: The gap-fill spot is usually even farther away.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You bought a Gap Support test. Ten trading days later it sits at 0.3R, never near 3R and never near the stop.
choices: Sell; under 1R after 10 trading days
Hold; the stop has not been hit
Add; it is holding the gap-up line
Move the stop to breakeven and wait
questions.answer: Sell; under 1R after 10 trading days
questions.why: Sell. Still under 1R after 10 trading days is the time stop. The stop is not hit, but the trade has not earned its place.
questions.lesson_line: A slow trade under 1R gets sold on day ten.

wrong.Hold; the stop has not been hit: The time stop exists for exactly this trade.
wrong.Add; it is holding the gap-up line: Adding breaks one buy, one price, one stop.
wrong.Move the stop to breakeven and wait: Breakeven comes at the first trim, not as a way to wait.

questions.q: Do you buy the close?
questions.story: The market reading is Red. A leader's test day holds the gap-up low, closes in the upper half, and the 50-day is rising.
choices: No; Red is mostly cash and shorts
Yes; great stocks ignore the market
Yes, at half size
Yes; Red allows an A+
questions.answer: No; Red is mostly cash and shorts
questions.why: No. In a Red market we are mostly in cash and short. Even a flawless test waits for the reading to improve.
questions.lesson_line: Red market: no new longs.

wrong.Yes; great stocks ignore the market: The reading is a guide for every long, leaders included.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size is for a weaker reading, not for Red.
wrong.Yes; Red allows an A+: Orange allows an A+. Red does not.

questions.q: Gap Support or PEG?
questions.story: A stock gapped 9% on earnings this morning and is holding near the high of the day. You are deciding which lesson owns today's buy.
choices: A PEG; the gap day is not Gap Support
Gap Support; the gap is holding
Gap Support; today's low is the line
Neither; wait for the report
questions.answer: A PEG; the gap day is not Gap Support
questions.why: A PEG. The gap day itself is a PEG, never Gap Support. Gap Support waits for price to come back to the gap-up low and defend it.
questions.lesson_line: Count the days since the gap. Day zero is a PEG.

wrong.Gap Support; the gap is holding: Holding today is the PEG day; Gap Support is a later test.
wrong.Gap Support; today's low is the line: Today's low is not yet a line that has been tested and defended.
wrong.Neither; wait for the report: The report already happened; that is why there is a gap.

questions.q: Gap Support or HVE line?
questions.story: Two marked lines sit near price. One is the low of the gap-up day. The other is the close of a record-volume day. You are asking which line this lesson defends.
choices: The gap-up day's low must hold
The record day's close must hold
Either one; they are the same
Neither; the 50-day decides
questions.answer: The gap-up day's low must hold
questions.why: The gap-up day's low must hold. Gap Support's line is the gap-up day's low and the gap must still be open. The HVE's line is the record-volume day's close, which price may trade under.
questions.lesson_line: Gap Support defends a low. The HVE defends a close.

wrong.The record day's close must hold: That is the HVE's line, and price may trade under it without harm.
wrong.Either one; they are the same: They are different setups with different lines.
wrong.Neither; the 50-day decides: The 50-day is a filter, not the line.

questions.q: Long, short, or neither?
questions.story: A stock gapped down off its highs. Weeks later price is rallying back up to the gap.
choices: Not Gap Support; a bear gap, no long
Long; the gap is support
Long; buy the rally into the gap
Gap Support; the stop goes over the gap
questions.answer: Not Gap Support; a bear gap, no long
questions.why: Not Gap Support. A bear gap is a gap down off the highs and is never a long. Gap Support is a gap up above a flat or rising 50-day whose low holds.
questions.lesson_line: A gap down is never a Gap Support long.

wrong.Long; the gap is support: A gap down is not support for a long.
wrong.Long; buy the rally into the gap: Buying a rally into a gap down is the opposite of this setup.
wrong.Gap Support; the stop goes over the gap: Gap Support is a gap up; its stop is under a low.

questions.q: Gap Support or Undercut and Rally?
questions.story: Price undercuts the lowest low of a base from five weeks ago and closes back over it two days later. No gap is involved.
choices: Undercut and Rally; no gap day
Gap Support; it undercut a low
A PEG; it reclaimed a swing low
A bear gap; it undercut a low
questions.answer: Undercut and Rally; no gap day
questions.why: An Undercut and Rally. It reclaims a prominent prior swing low within 3 sessions. Gap Support's undercut is of a gap-up day's low.
questions.lesson_line: Name the low that was undercut. A swing low is a U&R.

wrong.Gap Support; it undercut a low: Gap Support needs the undercut to be of a gap-up day's low.
wrong.A PEG; it reclaimed a swing low: A PEG is a report's reaction day, not a swing-low reclaim.
wrong.A bear gap; it undercut a low: A bear gap is a gap down; this had no gap.

questions.q: Grade each test.
questions.story: Two tests of two gaps. One holds the gap-up low to the tick and closes on a hammer. The other trades down to the prior day's high and reclaims the line by the close.
choices: First stronger; the fill is B- at best
Both the same; both closed back over
Second stronger; deeper means more fear
Both B-; any test is a B-
questions.answer: First stronger; the fill is B- at best
questions.why: First stronger; the fill is a B- at best. A fill to the gap-fill spot that reclaims the gap-up low is allowed but graded B- at best. The ranking is held, then a slight breach, then a fill that reclaims.
questions.lesson_line: Held beats a slight breach. A fill that reclaims is a B-.

wrong.Both the same; both closed back over: Both ended well, but the depth differs and the grade follows.
wrong.Second stronger; deeper means more fear: A deeper fill is weaker, not stronger.
wrong.Both B-; any test is a B-: A hold to the tick is the best version.

questions.q: Which grades higher, and why?
questions.story: Same clean test day on two stocks. One gapped 10% and the other gapped 35%.
choices: The 10% gap; a gap over 30% is lower
The 35% gap; bigger gaps are stronger
Neither; both are banned
The same; the test day decides
questions.answer: The 10% gap; a gap over 30% is lower
questions.why: The 10% gap. A gap over 30% is a lower grade, not a ban. Wagner: a gap of more than 30% could lead to a few months of chop.
questions.lesson_line: A gap over 30% grades lower, but it is not banned.

wrong.The 35% gap; bigger gaps are stronger: A very large gap tends to chop; it grades lower.
wrong.Neither; both are banned: A gap over 30% is a lower grade, not a ban.
wrong.The same; the test day decides: The gap size is part of the grade, even on a clean test.

questions.q: Grade each close.
questions.story: Two test days hold the gap-up low. One closes near its high on a hammer with a long lower wick. The other closes at 60% of its range.
choices: First an A+ cue; second is plain
Both the same; both held the line
First a B-; a hammer is a warning
Both A+; any hold is good enough
questions.answer: First an A+ cue; second is plain
questions.why: First an A+ cue, second a plain test. The A+ test closes back above the line near its high with a lower wick or hammer. A close in the upper half holds the line but earns no extra.
questions.lesson_line: A hammer close near the high is A+. Upper half just holds.

wrong.Both the same; both held the line: Both held, but the close is half the story.
wrong.First a B-; a hammer is a warning: A hammer with a lower wick is the best look.
wrong.Both A+; any hold is good enough: Only a close near the high is the A+ cue; 60% is not.

questions.q: Which pullback do traders like best?
questions.story: Two stocks pull back to the line. One drifts down on lighter volume. The other falls on heavy-volume selling.
choices: The quiet one on lighter volume
The heavy-volume one; it is a flush
Neither; volume does not matter
Both the same; the line decides
questions.answer: The quiet one on lighter volume
questions.why: The quiet one on lighter volume. Heavy-volume selling into the line is a warning, not a rule.
questions.lesson_line: Quiet pullbacks are the good ones.

wrong.The heavy-volume one; it is a flush: Heavy-volume selling into the line is a warning.
wrong.Neither; volume does not matter: Volume is a cue here, not noise.
wrong.Both the same; the line decides: The line matters, and so does how price gets there.

questions.q: Account 50,000. Risk 0.5%. Fill 53.27, stop 52.40. How many shares?
questions.why: 287. Account times risk percent, divided by the fill minus the stop, rounded down. The stop sets the size.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last.

questions.q: Where does the stop go?
questions.story: Midday on the test day, price undercuts the gap-up low and reclaims it on the 30-minute chart. You want to buy the reclaim.
choices: Just under the day's low so far
At the gap-fill spot, far below
Right on the gap-up low, exactly
No stop until the day's close
questions.answer: Just under the day's low so far
questions.why: A few cents under the test day's low so far. The intraday version is an undercut and reclaim, a red to green or an hourly higher low. It uses the same stop.
questions.lesson_line: Same stop on the intraday version.

wrong.At the gap-fill spot, far below: The gap-fill spot is usually far from the entry.
wrong.Right on the gap-up low, exactly: The stop sits a few cents under a low, not on the line.
wrong.No stop until the day's close: Every position has a real stop from the buy.

questions.q: Kacher and Morales allow a 1-2% undercut, so our stop is a fixed 1-3% under the gap-up low.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Kacher and Morales allow a 1 to 2% undercut in some cases. Our stop is a few cents under the test day's low, not a fixed 1% to 3% cushion.
questions.lesson_line: A real low sets the stop, not a fixed cushion.

questions.q: The gap day can close back inside the prior day's range and still count.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The gap day closes above the prior day's high. A gap that closes back inside the prior range has already given way.
questions.lesson_line: The gap day itself must close strong.

questions.q: The post-gap high is 24.00. The close before the test is 22.20. The 14-day ATR is 0.90. How many ATRs is the pullback?
questions.why: 2.0. The post-gap high minus the close before the test, divided by the ATR. That clears the 1 ATR minimum.
questions.lesson_line: Pullback depth is measured in ATRs.

questions.q: Take the test?
questions.story: A test day holds the gap-up low and closes in the upper half. The stock's RS rating is 52 and its group is one of the weakest.
choices: No; it is not a leader
Yes; the test is clean
Yes, at half size
Yes; the gap-up low is all that counts
questions.answer: No; it is not a leader
questions.why: No. Gap Support wants a leader: an RS rating of 80 or more, in a strong group. A clean test on a laggard is not enough.
questions.lesson_line: A leader first: RS 80 or more, in a strong group.

wrong.Yes; the test is clean: A clean chart on a laggard is not our setup.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size does not turn a laggard into a leader.
wrong.Yes; the gap-up low is all that counts: The line is one test; leadership is another.

questions.q: Buy the close?
questions.story: A test day holds the line and closes strong, but the close is 13% above the 10-day average.
choices: No; more than 10% over the 10-day
Yes; the test is textbook
Yes, at half size
Yes; the 10-day does not matter here
questions.answer: No; more than 10% over the 10-day
questions.why: No. At entry we take no more than 10% above the 10-day average. At 13% over, it is too stretched to buy.
questions.lesson_line: Skip a long more than 10% above its 10-day.

wrong.Yes; the test is textbook: A textbook chart still has to pass the stretch rule.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size does not fix a stretched entry.
wrong.Yes; the 10-day does not matter here: The stretch rule applies at the entry.

questions.q: Do you buy?
questions.story: A test day holds the gap-up low and closes in the upper half, but the close is under the 200-day.
choices: No; the test closed under the 200-day
Yes; the line held
Yes, at half size
Yes; the 50-day is rising
questions.answer: No; the test closed under the 200-day
questions.why: No. A test day that closes under the 200-day is off. No longs below the 200-day simple moving average.
questions.lesson_line: Under the 200-day, no buy.

wrong.Yes; the line held: Holding the line is not enough under the 200-day.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size does not fix a 200-day failure.
wrong.Yes; the 50-day is rising: A rising 50-day does not lift a close over the 200-day.

questions.q: What was that loss?
questions.story: AVGO, 2025. A 16.2% earnings gap on 4.3x volume. Thirteen sessions later the test day holds near perfectly, and you buy the close. The stop trades the next session.
choices: A planned loss; a clean test can lose
A mistake; the test was too clean
A mistake; you should have waited a day
A broken rule; the stop was too tight
questions.answer: A planned loss; a clean test can lose
questions.why: A planned loss; a clean test can still lose. The hold was near perfect, yet the stop traded the next session. The stop is the exit.
questions.lesson_line: The stop is the exit, even on a clean test.

wrong.A mistake; the test was too clean: A clean test is what we want; it cannot be a flaw.
wrong.A mistake; you should have waited a day: Waiting a day is not the rule; the test day is the signal.
wrong.A broken rule; the stop was too tight: The stop sat a few cents under the test day's low, as the rules say.

questions.q: What does the second close tell you?
questions.story: AEHR, 2023. The test day closes on the line with a hammer. The stop trades the next session. Two sessions later the stock closes under the gap-fill spot.
choices: The gap filled; the setup is dead
The line held; buy again
A fresh Gap Support; buy the close
A bounce is due; wait
questions.answer: The gap filled; the setup is dead
questions.why: The gap filled; the setup is dead. The hammer close on the line was fine, and the stop traded the next session. The later close under the gap-fill spot ended the setup.
questions.lesson_line: A close at the gap-fill spot ends it for good.

wrong.The line held; buy again: A close at the gap-fill spot means the line failed.
wrong.A fresh Gap Support; buy the close: A close under the gap-fill spot is a dead gap, not a fresh one.
wrong.A bounce is due; wait: Waiting for a bounce on a dead gap is hope.

questions.q: What was the missing filter?
questions.story: AMD, 2020. An 11.7% gap on 2.2x volume. Thirty-five sessions later the test closes at 97% of its range. The stop trades with no gain. The broad market was pulling back.
choices: The market reading
The gap size
The test-day close
The stop distance
questions.answer: The market reading
questions.why: The market reading. The test closed at 97% of its range, yet the broad market was in a pullback. The scan ignores the market reading; the rulebook does not.
questions.lesson_line: A great test in a weak market is still a weak trade.

wrong.The gap size: An 11.7% gap is not the problem.
wrong.The stop distance: The stop sat under the test day's low.

questions.q: Take it or pass?
questions.story: DE, 2026. A 6.8% gap on 4.4x volume. Four sessions later the test closes at 0.01 of its range, 0.8% under the line.
choices: Pass; still falling into the close
Take it; it is only 0.8% under
Take it; the gap is open
Take it; the volume was huge
questions.answer: Pass; still falling into the close
questions.why: Pass. The test closed at 0.01 of its range, 0.8% under the line. A day still falling into the close, with no hold and no reclaim, is not the setup.
questions.lesson_line: A test that closes at its low is not a hold.

wrong.Take it; it is only 0.8% under: A close at the low is not a hold, however small the miss.
wrong.Take it; the gap is open: An open gap is one test; the hold is another.
wrong.Take it; the volume was huge: Volume on the gap day does not rescue a weak test.

questions.q: Take it or pass?
questions.story: DOCU, 2025. A 9.1% gap on 5.4x volume closed 2.6% under a falling 50-day. Eleven sessions later the test looks fine.
choices: Pass; the gap is in a downtrend
Take it; the test day looks clean
Take it; 5.4x volume is huge
Take it; the gap is still open
questions.answer: Pass; the gap is in a downtrend
questions.why: Pass. The gap day closed under a falling 50-day. The test looked fine, but it was a bounce in a downtrend. No downtrend gaps.
questions.lesson_line: A clean test in a downtrend is still a bounce.

wrong.Take it; the test day looks clean: A clean test does not cancel the downtrend.
wrong.Take it; 5.4x volume is huge: Heavy volume does not turn a downtrend gap into a leader.
wrong.Take it; the gap is still open: An open gap is not enough under a falling 50-day.

questions.q: Take it or pass?
questions.story: EVR, 2019. An 11.3% gap on 4.1x volume above a rising 50-day. Six sessions later the test closes 6.9% under the 200-day.
choices: Pass; it closed under the 200-day
Take it; the 50-day is still rising
Take it; the gap is huge on volume
Take it, but at half size
questions.answer: Pass; it closed under the 200-day
questions.why: Pass. The test closed 6.9% under the 200-day. The gap, the rising 50-day and the test all passed, but no longs below the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: Everything can pass but the 200-day. Pass.

wrong.Take it; the 50-day is still rising: The 50-day does not lift a close over the 200-day.
wrong.Take it; the gap is huge on volume: Gap size does not change the 200-day rule.
wrong.Take it, but at half size: Half size does not fix a 200-day failure.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You bought at 20.00 with the stop at 19.40. A report gaps it down to 18.70, and the first 30-minute bar's low is 18.50.
choices: Get out; the loss is past 2R
Stop at 18.50 and wait
Stop at 19.40; it will bounce
Add at 18.50 to lower your cost
questions.answer: Get out; the loss is past 2R
questions.why: Get out. On a gap through the stop, the first 30-minute low is the new stop. Here that loss is past 2R, so you are out.
questions.lesson_line: Past 2R in the first half hour, get out.

wrong.Stop at 18.50 and wait: The first 30-minute low is the new stop only while the loss is within 2R.
wrong.Stop at 19.40; it will bounce: The old stop is gone, and waiting for a bounce is hope.
wrong.Add at 18.50 to lower your cost: Adding breaks one buy, one price, one stop.

questions.q: By our plan, where does the first third go?
questions.story: LLY, 2021. A news gap. The test is bought at 231.13 with the stop at 228.43. The post-gap high is 239.37.
choices: At the post-gap high, 239.37
At 5R
Only after the close above 240
questions.why: At 3R, 239.23. One R is the fill minus the stop. Three of those above 231.13 is 239.23, a hair under the post-gap high of 239.37. The post-gap high is no earlier cue here.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R. The post-gap high only helps when it comes first.

wrong.At the post-gap high, 239.37: The post-gap high sits above 3R. It is a cue only when it comes before 3R.
wrong.At 5R: The first third comes off before 5R.
wrong.Only after the close above 240: There is no rule to wait for 240.

questions.q: May you take it?
questions.story: You were stopped out of the same gap-up low three times this week. On Friday it tests the line again and closes strong.
choices: No; three tries this week are used
Yes; a new trigger is a new trade
Yes, at double size to make it back
Yes, with a wider stop this time
questions.answer: No; three tries this week are used
questions.why: No. At most 3 tries a week and 6 a month on the same line. After a stop-out, buy again only on a new trigger.
questions.lesson_line: Three tries a week on one line, then stop.

wrong.Yes; a new trigger is a new trade: A new trigger is a new trade, but the tries per week are capped.
wrong.Yes, at double size to make it back: Doubling size to win it back breaks the sizing rule.
wrong.Yes, with a wider stop this time: A wider stop breaks the stop rule.

questions.q: A gap that is never revisited is nothing; the setup is the later test.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A gap that is never revisited is nothing. The setup is the later test of the gap-up low.
questions.lesson_line: No test, no setup.

questions.q: Which order ranks the tests, best to worst?
choices: Held, slight breach, fill that reclaims
Fill that reclaims, held, slight breach
Slight breach, held, fill that reclaims
All three grade the same
questions.answer: Held, slight breach, fill that reclaims
questions.why: Held, slight breach, fill that reclaims. A fill that reclaims the gap-up low is allowed but graded B- at best.
questions.lesson_line: Held, then a slight breach, then a fill that reclaims.

wrong.Fill that reclaims, held, slight breach: A fill that reclaims is the weakest of the three, not the best.
wrong.Slight breach, held, fill that reclaims: Holding to the tick ranks above a slight breach.
wrong.All three grade the same: The ranking is held first, and the fill is the lesser grade.

questions.q: Which test is the weaker one?
questions.story: Test A comes after six weeks of chop sitting on the line. Test B comes seven weeks after the gap, a clean 15% slide straight back to the line.
choices: A; weeks of chop on the line is B-
B; seven weeks is too late to buy
Both the same; time does not matter
B; a 15% slide back is a failure
questions.answer: A; weeks of chop on the line is B-
questions.why: A. Weeks of chop sitting on the line before the test is a B- cue. A long drift back to the line is not a minus by itself.
questions.lesson_line: Chop on the line is a B- cue. A long drift is not.

wrong.B; seven weeks is too late to buy: A long drift back to the line is not a minus by itself.
wrong.Both the same; time does not matter: AXON's test came 35 sessions after the gap and worked.
wrong.B; a 15% slide back is a failure: A slide that stops on the line is the pullback.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You bought the test day's close. A friend says you can watch the stop by hand since you are at your screen all day.
choices: Place the stop order with the broker now
Watch it by hand today
Use a mental stop under the low
Set it tomorrow after the open
questions.answer: Place the stop order with the broker now
questions.why: Place the stop order with the broker now. Every position has a real stop order with the broker, not a stop kept in your head. It only moves up.
questions.lesson_line: A real stop order, placed with the buy.

wrong.Watch it by hand today: A stop in your head is not a stop; screens fail and moods change.
wrong.Use a mental stop under the low: A mental stop is the same mistake.
wrong.Set it tomorrow after the open: The risk starts at the buy; so does the stop order.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the test day is the last bar. Did it hold the gap-up low and close back strong? Buy the close or pass.
choices: Take it; it held and closed high
Pass; the gap has already filled
Pass; it closed in the lower half
questions.answer: Take it; it held and closed high
questions.why: Take it. A quiet stock gapped on 11.5x volume. Five sessions later the low dipped 0.3% under the line. The day closed at 62% of its range, with the gap still open.
questions.lesson_line: A hold at the line with a strong close is the setup.

wrong.Pass; the gap has already filled: No close sat at or under the gap-fill spot.
wrong.Pass; it closed in the lower half: The close was in the upper half of its range.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the test day is the last bar. Did it hold the line and close back strong? Buy the close or pass.
choices: Pass; it closed at its low
Take it; it held the line today
Take it; the gap is open
questions.answer: Pass; it closed at its low
questions.why: Pass. The test closed at 0.01 of its range, 0.8% under the line. A day still falling into the close is not the setup.
questions.lesson_line: A test that closes at its low is not a hold.

wrong.Take it; it held the line today: It closed under the line, not on it.
wrong.Take it; the gap is open: An open gap is not enough; the day has to hold.

questions.q: Grade this one.
questions.story: A leader, RS 85, growing sales and earnings. It gapped 10% on 4x volume. Eight sessions later a quiet pullback tags the line to the tick and closes near its high on a hammer. The stop is 2.1% away in a Green market.
choices: A+; the cues line up
B-; the gap is only 10%
B-; the test came late
No trade; it needs a deeper undercut
questions.answer: A+; the cues line up
questions.why: A+. A leader with growing sales and earnings, a heavy-volume gap and a quiet first test that holds the line to the tick. Add a hammer close, risk under 3% and a Green market.
questions.lesson_line: When every cue lines up, it is an A+.

wrong.B-; the gap is only 10%: A gap of 10% or more on heavy volume is a strong cue, not a weakness.
wrong.B-; the test came late: Eight sessions is early, and a long drift is not a minus anyway.
wrong.No trade; it needs a deeper undercut: A hold to the tick is the best test, not a flaw.

questions.q: Why trade it at all?
questions.story: Bulkowski found that gaps in an uptrend show underlying support only 20% of the time in a bull market. A member asks why we trade Gap Support at all.
choices: Leaders, the right line, a tight stop
Gaps always fill, so fade every one
Volume on the gap day guarantees support
Ignore Bulkowski; he is wrong
questions.answer: Leaders, the right line, a tight stop
questions.why: Pick leaders, the right line and the market, and keep a tight stop. Bulkowski found gaps in an uptrend show support only 20% of the time, and in our scan 28.9% reached 3R. The edge is the stock, the level and the market, with small stops, not a promise.
questions.lesson_line: No guarantees: leader, line, market, and a tight stop.

wrong.Gaps always fill, so fade every one: Our rule is that buyable gaps do not fill, and we do not fade them.
wrong.Ignore Bulkowski; he is wrong: His count is a fair warning, not an error to ignore.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: DKS, 2021. You bought the test and the stop traded the next session on a 2.4% undercut that closed back on the line. Weeks later the stock has run far higher.
choices: Nothing; wait for a new trigger
Chase it; you were right all along
Rebuy at double size next time
Widen your stops on the next buy
questions.answer: Nothing; wait for a new trigger
questions.why: Nothing now. The stop is the exit, and a re-entry needs a new trigger. The stop traded on a 2.4% undercut that closed back on the line, and the stock then ran. That is hindsight, not a mistake.
questions.lesson_line: A stop that was right by the rules stays right.

wrong.Chase it; you were right all along: Chasing is how a planned small loss becomes a bigger one.
wrong.Rebuy at double size next time: Doubling size to win it back breaks the sizing rule.
wrong.Widen your stops on the next buy: Wider stops break the stop rule.
